exercises.heading: 16.8. Exercises

problem.paragraph: A disk $$D$$ , a hemisphere $$H$$ , and a portion $$P$$ of a paraboloid are shown. Suppose $$\mathbf{F}$$ is a vector field on $${\mathbb{R}}^{3}$$ whose components have continuous partial derivatives. Explain why this statement is true:
$$\iint\limits_{D}{curl}\mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = {\iint\limits_{H}{{curl}\mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{S}}} = {\iint\limits_{P}{{curl}\mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{S}}}$$

image.alt: Details The figure has three parts. In all three parts, a curved surface is graphed in the x y z coordinate plane. The positive x-axis slopes down and to the left. The positive x axis has a single tick mark labeled 2. The positive y-axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive x axis has a single tick mark labeled 2. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. The positive x axis has a single tick mark labeled 4. In the first part, a circle is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The circle lies on the x y plane with its center at the origin and crosses the positive x and y axes at (2, 0, 0) and (0, 2, 0), respectively. The region within the circle is labeled D. In the second part, a three-dimensional rendering of a hemisphere, labeled H, is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The base of the hemisphere is a circle lying on the x y plane, with its center at the origin, crossing the positive x and y axes at (2, 0, 0) and (0, 2, 0), respectively. The topmost point of the hemisphere is on the positive z-axis. In the third part, a three-dimensional rendering of a paraboloid, labeled P, is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The base of the paraboloid is a circle lying on the x y plane, with its center at the origin, crossing the positive x and y axes at (2, 0, 0) and (0, 2, 0), respectively. The vertex of the paraboloid is at (0, 0, 4).

exercises.paragraph: 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6, Use Stokes’ Theorem to evaluate $$\iint_{S}{{curl}\mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{S}}$$ .

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = x^{2}\sin z\mathbf{i} + y^{2}\mathbf{j} + xy\mathbf{k}$$ , $$S$$ is the part of the paraboloid $$z = 1 - x^{2} - y^{2}$$ that lies above the $$xy$$ -plane, oriented upward

$$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = ze^{ y}\mathbf{i} + x\cos y\mathbf{j} + xz\sin y\mathbf{k}$$ , $$S$$ is the hemisphere $${x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 16},{y \geqslant 0}$$ , oriented in the direction of the positive $$y$$ -axis

$$\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = \tan^{- 1}(x^{2}yz^{2})\mathbf{i} + x^{2}y\mathbf{j} + x^{2}z^{2}\mathbf{k}$$ , $$S$$ is the cone $${x = \sqrt{y^{2} + z^{2}}},{0 \leqslant x \leqslant 2}$$ , oriented in the direction of the positive $$x$$ -axis

$$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = xyz\mathbf{i} + xy\mathbf{j} + x^{2}yz\mathbf{k}$$ , $$S$$ consists of the top and the four sides (but not the bottom) of the cube with vertices $$\left( {\pm 1, \pm 1, \pm 1} \right)$$ , oriented outward

$$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = e^{ xy}\mathbf{i} + e^{ xz}\mathbf{j} + x^{2}z\mathbf{k}$$ , $$S$$ is the half of the ellipsoid $$4x^{2} + y^{2} + 4z^{2} = 4$$ that lies to the right of the $$xz$$ -plane, oriented in the direction of the positive $$y$$ -axis

image.alt: Details A three-dimensional rendering of a paraboloid is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the right. The positive y axis slopes slightly up and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. The paraboloid, labeled S and defined by 4 x^2 + y^2 + 4 z^2 = 4, is symmetric about the positive y axis with its vertex on the positive y axis, and its base lies on the x z plane.

exercises.paragraph: 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, and 14 Use Stokes’ Theorem to evaluate $$\int_{C}{\mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r}}$$ . In each case $$C$$ is oriented counterclockwise as viewed from above, unless otherwise stated.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = {({x + y^{2}})}\mathbf{i} + {({y + z^{2}})}\mathbf{j} + {({z + x^{2}})}\mathbf{k}$$ , $$C$$ is the triangle with vertices $$(1,0,0)$$ , $$(0,1,0)$$ and $$(0,0,1)$$

$$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = \mathbf{i} + \left( {x + yz} \right)\mathbf{j} + \left( {xy - \sqrt{z}} \right)\mathbf{k}$$ , $$C$$ is the boundary of the part of the plane $$3x + 2y + z = 1$$ in the first octant
$$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = xy\mathbf{i} + yz\mathbf{j} + zx\mathbf{k}$$ , $$C$$ is the boundary of the part of the paraboloid $$z = 1 - x^{2} - y^{2}$$ in the first octant

image.alt: Details A curved surface is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. The boundary of the curved surface, labeled C, resembles a curved triangle with its vertices on the positive x, y, and z axes. An arrowhead is placed on each side of the triangle and they all point counterclockwise. The curved surface labeled z = 1 minus x^2 minus y^2 bulges away from the origin.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = 2y\mathbf{i} + xz\mathbf{j} + \left( {x + y} \right)\mathbf{k}$$ , $$C$$ is the curve of intersection of the plane $$z = y + 2$$ and the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 1$$
$$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = \langle - yx^{2},xy^{2},e^{\mathit{xy}}\rangle$$ , $$C$$ is the circle in the $$\mathit{xy}$$ -plane of radius $$2$$ centered at the origin

$$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = ze^{x}\mathbf{i} + (z - y^{3})\mathbf{j} + (x - z^{3})\mathbf{k}$$ , $$C$$ is the circle $$y^{2} + z^{2} = 4$$ , $$x = 3$$ , oriented clockwise as viewed from the origin

$$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = x^{2}y\mathbf{i} + x^{3}\mathbf{j} + e^{z}\tan^{- 1}z\mathbf{k}$$ , $$C$$ is the curve with parametric equations $$x = \cos t$$ , $$y = \sin t$$ , $$z = \sin t$$ , $$0 \leqslant t \leqslant 2\pi$$

image.alt: Details A closed curve and a shaded region are graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. The curve, labeled C, resembles an ellipse sloping upward to the right with its center at the origin and crosses the x axis at (negative 1, 0, 0) and (1, 0, 0). Two arrowheads were placed on the curve point counterclockwise. The region within the curve is shaded.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = \langle x^{3} - z,\mathit{xy},y + z^{2}\rangle$$ , $$C$$ is the curve of intersection of the paraboloid $$z = x^{2} + y^{2}$$ and the plane $$z = x$$

image.alt: Details A three-dimensional rendering of a paraboloid, a plane, and a closed curve is graphed in the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. The paraboloid, labeled z = x^2 + y^2, has its vertex at the origin and opens upward. The plane, labeled z = x, slopes upward to the left and the front, above the first and fourth quadrants of the x y plane. The closed curve lies on the plane and resembles a circle with its bottom-most point at the origin. Two arrowheads were placed on the curve point clockwise.

list.item: Use Stokes’ Theorem to evaluate $$\int_{C}{\mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r}}$$ , where $$\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) = x^{2}z\mathbf{i} + xy^{2}\mathbf{j} + z^{2}\mathbf{k}$$ and $$C$$ is the curve of intersection of the plane $$x + y + z = 1$$ and the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 9$$ , oriented counterclockwise as viewed from above.
Graph both the plane and the cylinder with domains chosen so that you can see the curve $$C$$ and the surface that you used in part (a).
Find parametric equations for $$C$$ and use them to graph $$C$$ .

Use Stokes’ Theorem to evaluate $$\int_{C}{\mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r}}$$ , where $$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = x^{2}y\mathbf{i} + \frac{1}{3}x^{3}\mathbf{j} + xy\mathbf{k}$$ and $$C$$ is the curve of intersection of the hyperbolic paraboloid $$z = y^{2} - x^{2}$$ and the cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 1$$ , oriented counterclockwise as viewed from above.
Graph both the hyperbolic paraboloid and the cylinder with domains chosen so that you can see the curve $$C$$ and the surface that you used in part (a).
Find parametric equations for $$C$$ and use them to graph $$C$$ .

exercises.paragraph: 17, 18, and 19 Verify that Stokes’ Theorem is true for the given vector field $$\mathbf{F}$$ and surface $$S$$ .

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = - y\mathbf{i} + x\mathbf{j} - 2\mathbf{k}$$ , $$S$$ is the cone $${z^{2} = x^{2} + y^{2}},{0 \leqslant z \leqslant 4}$$ , oriented downward

$$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = - 2yz\mathbf{i} + y\mathbf{j} + 3x\mathbf{k}$$ , $$S$$ is the part of the paraboloid $$z = 5 - x^{2} - y^{2}$$ that lies above the plane $$z = 1$$ , oriented upward

$$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = y\mathbf{i} + z\mathbf{j} + x\mathbf{k}$$ , $$S$$ is the hemisphere $${x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 1},{y \geqslant 0}$$ , oriented in the direction of the positive $$y$$ -axis
Let $$C$$ be a simple closed smooth curve that lies in the plane $$x + y + z = 1$$ . Show that the line integral
$$\int_{C}{zdx - 2xdy + 3ydz}$$
depends only on the area of the region enclosed by $$C$$ and not on the shape of $$C$$ or its location in the plane.

A particle moves along line segments from the origin to the points $$\left( {1,0,0} \right)$$ , $$\left( {1,2,1} \right)$$ , $$\left( {0,2,1} \right)$$ , and back to the origin under the influence of the force field
$$\mathbf{F}\left( {x,y,z} \right) = z^{2}\mathbf{i} + 2xy\mathbf{j} + 4y^{2}\mathbf{k}$$
Find the work done.
Evaluate
$$\int_{C}{\left( {y + \sin x} \right)dx + {({z^{2} + \cos y})}dy + x^{3}dz}$$
where $$C$$ is the curve $${\mathbf{r}(t) = {\langle{\sin t,\cos t,\sin 2t}\rangle}},{0 \leqslant t \leqslant 2\pi}$$ .
[Hint: Observe that $$C$$ lies on the surface $$z = 2xy$$ .]
If $$S$$ is a sphere and $$\mathbf{F}$$ satisfies the hypotheses of Stokes’ Theorem, show that $$\iint_{S}{{curl}\mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = 0}$$ .
Suppose $$S$$ and $$C$$ satisfy the hypotheses of Stokes’ Theorem and $$f$$ , $$g$$ have continuous second-order partial derivatives. Use Exercises 26 and 28 in Section 16.5 to show the following.
